newsitem.title: USA: Oregon unemployment rate rose to 5.8 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Oregon unemployment rate rose to 5.8 pct in March.

text.p: Oregon's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose two-tenth of a percentage point to 5.8 percent in March, the state's Employment Department said on Tuesday.

"The rate of job growth in Oregon is slowing," said David Cooke, an economist with the Employment Department. "Since December, annualized nonfarm job growth is 2.2 percent, a slowdown from the four percent annual growth rates the state has achieved over the past three calendar years."
Oregon's unemployment rate was 5.5 percent in January and 5.6 percent in February, the department said.
The Employment Department said its monthly survey of businesses showed an unusual trend in March. Employment declined for the first time since February 1996, the department said.

In March, seasonally adjusted job declines were recorded in construction, services and government. Trade and manufacturing were the only major sectors showing significant positive job gains, the department said.
